record.title: Public identity routes bypass the configured throttle before password work
record.description: Small valid unauthenticated registration requests trigger Argon2id hashing and Account insertion, while login requests naming an existing Account trigger password verification even when the password is wrong. AccountController does not use the configured ThrottlerGuard, although the sibling public OAuth token route explicitly installs it, so the omission is localized rather than a property of the throttler setup. If upstream admission and Bun's effective worker/queue controls do not protect the shared API budget, anonymous password work could reduce availability for other Organizations. The source establishes the admission gap and input-to-work path, not a measured service outage or unbounded native worker count.
record.claimed_root_cause: ThrottlerModule is configured without a global guard, and the public identity controller omits the per-route guard that OAuth token exchange explicitly installs. The identity service submits password work without a source-visible per-IP/global work budget or submission bound. Per-field and parser size limits do not stop repeated small requests. Runtime worker limits and deployed upstream controls may constrain the impact and are not assumed absent.

trace.description: Public registration and the adjacent auth/login handler accept requests without an authentication or throttle guard.
A configured throttler does not cover these routes automatically: AppModule registers no APP_GUARD and the identity module provides no alternative admission guard.
A short syntactically valid email and 12-to-256-character password pass validation; a large request body is unnecessary.
An unused email passes the uniqueness lookup and reaches password hashing without a submission budget. Repeated unique emails avoid the duplicate-account early exit.

Registration submits Argon2id work to Bun.password.hash followed by durable Account creation; the independent existing-email login variant submits Bun.password.verify at line 92. These costs occur in the shared API process before successful authentication.

evidence.description: Neither public identity handler has ThrottlerGuard; protected handlers explicitly declare their AccountAuthGuard.
The application configures a rate limit but does not install it globally; providers contain only RulesService and PolicyContextService, with no APP_GUARD.
The sibling public OAuth token route explicitly installs ThrottlerGuard, showing the guard-based enforcement used elsewhere.
An accepted unused email causes Argon2id hashing followed by durable Account creation via PrismaIdentityRepo.addAccount.
A known email causes password verification even when the attempt will return UnauthorizedException; unknown emails short-circuit before this cost.
Input length limits are effective per request but do not bound aggregate submissions or work already admitted.
The optional support API publishes on loopback. This is a visible reachability constraint; public routing and any upstream work limits cannot be inferred from this scaffold.

blockers: No bounded admission fixture or native password-cost observation was run because target execution is prohibited without complete OS memory and cumulative disk controls.

The effective upstream rate/concurrency limits, reachable identity-route topology, Bun password-worker queue/concurrency bounds and shared API resource budget are not established by source; the Kubernetes and Helm definitions are incomplete scaffolds with no ingress or rate-limit configuration. Without them, a meaningful cross-Organization availability effect cannot be asserted.

validation_plan.local: Once a complete sandbox is available, configure a dummy identity application with a rate limit of one and replace password hashing/verification with bounded deferred mocks. Submit only two small requests per registration/login variant and record whether the second reaches the password-work mock or is rejected before admission. Inspect worker/queue configuration rather than stressing real Argon2. Use a separately bounded dummy request to determine which resources are shared, then stop; do not perform saturation testing.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner should inspect the actual API ingress or local caller boundary, per-IP and aggregate admission policy, Bun password-work queue limits, and API CPU/memory isolation. Establish whether those controls cap anonymous admitted work below the shared resource budget and how pending work is cleared. This is a configuration and capacity review, not a request to send traffic to a deployed service.
